text:
SRE Bot: INCIDENT ALERT — kv-cache growth abnormality detected in continuous-batching pool (region-us-west). Error rate spike +120% since 2076543000. paging oncall: @Trent (oncall) :rotating_light:

Trent (oncall): on it, looking at dashboards now. which tenant slice?

SRE Bot: hot-shard: tenant-slice 42; tail latency > 2s for 95th, evictions up. logs: `kv.evictions.rate` and `batch.window.size` trending upward.

Alex K.: saw this — we've been rolling batch-window decrease flag earlier today. could be misconfigured rolling window amplification with prefix caching.

Maya R.: confirming impact: customer-facing error retries for a subset of customers (slice 42 & 57). CS says 3 customers reported timeouts. @Customer Success please collect customer ids.

Customer Success: Received 3 reports — cust-alpha, cust-gamma, cust-delta. They're seeing degraded generation times and some 502s.

Trent (oncall): starting live mitigation: plan = 1) revert batch-window flag to safe default globally, 2) if that causes unhealthy throughput, apply per-customer override for affected tenants, 3) run canary for reduced batch-size on 2 hosts. Rolling with step 1 now.

DeployBot: deploy request queued: `flag:batch_window_ms -> 20` -> `flag:batch_window_ms -> 50` rollback. initiating change across region-us-west.

Alex K.: wait — full revert global might spike costs due to smaller batches. prefer per-customer overrides first for the three reported customers while we root-cause. can we toggle per-tenant flag quickly?

Trent (oncall): good point. switching to per-customer overrides instead. executing commands:

```
# per-tenant override via feature flag service
ffctl set tenant:cust-alpha batch_window_ms=20 --region us-west
ffctl set tenant:cust-gamma batch_window_ms=20 --region us-west
ffctl set tenant:cust-delta batch_window_ms=20 --region us-west
```

SRE Bot: feature flag changes applied (3 tenants). Propagation ~ 30s.

Maya R.: monitoring metrics for those tenants — 30s and counting. tail latency for cust-alpha dropped from 2.4s -> 0.6s on first host sample. errors decreasing. :white_check_mark:

Alex K.: good. while per-tenant is stabilizing, let's snapshot KV metrics and start a short canary of smaller continuous-batch size to validate root cause. schedule canary on 2 instances with traffic diversion 5% each.

Trent (oncall): canary launched: `canary-id: c-canary-2076` routing 5% slices for 15m, batch_window_ms=15, kv-cache GC tuning set to conservative.

SRE Bot: canary health at 5m: success indicators positive (error rate down 80% vs baseline on slices). No CPU/memory anomalies.

Maya R.: Meanwhile CS contacted cust-delta who confirmed recovery. advising continued monitoring.

Alex K.: digging into traces: sequences show unusual KV cache growth on long-running sessions — prefix reuse interacts poorly with the new aggressive batch-window (batches containing many unique keys causing KV pressure). suspect batching window mis-size leads to cache amplification.

Trent (oncall): mitigation summary so far: 1) Per-tenant overrides for reported customers applied; 2) Canary for batch reduction healthy; 3) holding global flag rollback pending post-mortem (avoid cost shock).

Ops Runbook: please file incident with labels: kv-cache, continuous-batching, per-tenant-override, canary. Assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml for root cause.

Maya R.: will create postmortem doc and add link here. immediate follow-ups: - ensure auto-scaling headroom for canary hosts - add a safeguard to flag service to prevent global rolling to aggressive batch_window without gating metrics - add tenant-level monitoring alert for eviction spikes.

Trent (oncall): handing off to next oncall. Handoff notes: per-tenant overrides in place for 3 customers, canary running c-canary-2076, monitoring thresholds adjusted. Pager escalations suppressed for this slice. @Alex K. and @Maya R. will lead RCA.

DeployBot: handoff recorded by incident-bot at 2076543299.

Alex K.: thanks — will include repro steps and telemetry samples in the postmortem. tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml. good catch team. :thumbsup:
